decks.domain: Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals

cards.front: What do solid white fog lines mark, and may you cross them to pass?
cards.back: Solid white fog lines mark the right edge of the road and help you stay on it at night or in bad weather, and crossing them to pass is illegal.

cards.front: Where do solid white lines separate lanes, and should you cross them?
cards.back: Solid white lines also separate same-direction lanes where lane changes are risky, such as sharp curves and freeway acceleration and deceleration lanes, and you should not cross them.

cards.front: What does a double solid white line separate, and may you cross it?
cards.back: A double solid white line separates two same-direction travel paths, and crossing it is prohibited.

cards.front: How are crosswalks marked?
cards.back: Crosswalks are marked by solid white lines painted across the pavement or by white stripes laid in the direction of traffic, at intersections and sometimes midblock.

cards.front: Where do you stop at a crosswalk?
cards.back: Stop behind the crosswalk line.

cards.front: What does a stop line show?
cards.back: A stop line is a wide white line across a lane showing where to stop at an intersection, keeping you clear of pedestrians and cross traffic.

cards.front: Where do you stop when there is no stop line or crosswalk?
cards.back: With no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection, and in every case make sure you can see traffic from all directions before going.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals

cards.front: What do wide white arrows in a lane show?
cards.back: Wide white arrows down the middle of a lane show the movements allowed from it; in the handbook example the far-right lane is right turn only, the next lane allows right or straight, and turning right from the other two lanes is illegal.

cards.front: Who may use a bicycle lane?
cards.back: A bicycle lane, shown by special markings and signs, is reserved only for bicyclists.

cards.front: What does green paint in a bike lane flag?
cards.back: Green paint in a bike lane flags a likely conflict point between cars and bicycles, usually at intersections and driveways, so take extra care turning there.

cards.front: Which actions are illegal in a bike lane?
cards.back: Driving, passing, turning right, parking, pulling over to wait, or making a delivery in a bike lane is illegal.

cards.front: What do shared lane markings tell you?
cards.back: Shared lane markings show proper lane position and traffic flow, and when you see one, watch for bicyclists and give them room as legal road users.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals

cards.front: What do yellow lines separate, and what types are there?
cards.back: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and come as solid, broken and center-lane lines.

cards.front: What does a single broken yellow center line usually allow?
cards.back: A single broken yellow center line on a two-way road usually means you may pass when it is safe.

cards.front: May you cross a solid yellow line on your side to pass?
cards.back: Do not cross a solid yellow line on your side of the center line to pass.

cards.front: Where does a solid yellow line mark the left edge?
cards.back: On a four-lane divided road or a one-way road, a solid yellow line usually marks the pavement's left edge.

cards.front: What does a double solid yellow center line ban, and when may you cross it?
cards.back: A double solid yellow center line on a two-lane road bans passing in both directions, though you may cross it to turn into a driveway or crossroad or reach a parking spot.

cards.front: How is a left-turn-only center lane marked, and who may use it?
cards.back: A left-turn-only center lane has solid yellow lines on its outer edges and broken yellow lines inside, and left turns may be made from it in either direction.

cards.front: May you use the center turn lane to pass or merge?
cards.back: Using the left-turn-only center lane to pass or merge is illegal and dangerous.

cards.front: How do the lines of a center turn lane read, and what is it never for?
cards.back: A left-turn-only center lane has solid yellow lines on its outer edges and broken yellow lines on its inner edges, and it serves left turns from either direction but never passing or merging.

cards.front: How do broken, solid and double solid yellow lines differ for passing?
cards.back: A broken yellow center line allows passing when safe, but a solid yellow line on your side forbids it, and a double solid yellow forbids it for both directions.

cards.front: What does every type of yellow line have in common?
cards.back: Any yellow line, whether solid, broken or a center-lane line, separates traffic moving in opposite directions.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals

cards.front: What is a Michigan Left?
cards.back: Michigan Lefts, or indirect left turns, have been used since the late 1960s; where they exist you cannot turn left directly but drive straight or turn right and then U-turn at a median crossover.

cards.front: How many vehicles fit a single-lane crossover, and why is it wide?
cards.back: A single-lane Michigan Left crossover takes one vehicle at a time; extra width is there for tractor trailers and RVs that need a wider turn.

cards.front: When may two vehicles turn together at a crossover?
cards.back: A multi-lane Michigan Left lets two vehicles turn together when arrows, ONLY lettering and solid white lines show it, and an unmarked crossover is always treated as single-lane.

cards.front: How do you make a Michigan Left from the main highway?
cards.back: From the main highway, drive past the intersection, turn left into the median crossover, then turn left back onto the main highway when clear, and then either keep going straight or get into the far-right lane to make a right onto the cross road.

cards.front: How do you make a Michigan Left from the cross road?
cards.back: From the cross road, turn right onto the main highway, move to the far-left lane, turn left into the median crossover, and when clear turn left onto the main highway and continue straight.

cards.front: How do you treat an unmarked Michigan Left crossover?
cards.back: A Michigan Left crossover with no markings is always single-lane, even if it looks wide enough for two cars, because that width is for large vehicles.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals

cards.front: Where do yield lines appear, and where do you stop?
cards.back: Yield lines appear at roundabouts and midblock crosswalks, and when yielding you stop behind them.

cards.front: What do white triangles across a lane mean?
cards.back: White triangles painted across a lane mean be ready to stop and yield to pedestrians.

cards.front: What do dashed white lines across a roundabout lane mark?
cards.back: Dashed white lines across a lane in a roundabout mark the edge of its circular lane.

cards.front: May you cut through a parking lot to avoid a traffic signal?
cards.back: Driving through a store parking lot or any other public or private property to get around a traffic-control device is illegal.

cards.front: How do white triangles differ from dashed white lines in a roundabout?
cards.back: White triangles across a lane are pedestrian yield lines, while dashed white lines across a roundabout lane mark the edge of the circle.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals

cards.front: What does a red light mean?
cards.back: A red light, at the top of Michigan signals, means stop behind the crosswalk or stop line.

cards.front: What does a yellow light require?
cards.back: A yellow light means the signal is about to turn red, and you are required to stop; when a safe stop is impossible, do not accelerate, and go through the intersection with caution.

cards.front: What does a green light mean?
cards.back: A green light means proceed with caution after checking for pedestrians and vehicles.

cards.front: What do you do at a signal that is not working?
cards.back: If a signal is not working and no officer or other device controls traffic, stop completely, yield to vehicles already there, and yield to the right on a tie.

cards.front: What must you do at a red light before moving on?
cards.back: At a red light, stop completely and check cross traffic and pedestrians before moving on green or turning right on red.

cards.front: What does a flashing red light mean?
cards.back: A flashing red light means come to a full stop and go only when the road is clear.

cards.front: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
cards.back: A flashing yellow light means go through the intersection carefully, scanning cross traffic both ways.

cards.front: How does a steady yellow differ from a flashing yellow light?
cards.back: A steady yellow on a doghouse signal means stop if you have not entered the intersection, whereas a flashing yellow light lets you continue carefully through it.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals

cards.front: What does a doghouse signal control?
cards.back: The five-section-head or doghouse signal controls turns with red, yellow and green lights plus a yellow and a green turn arrow.

cards.front: How does a green arrow differ from a green light on a doghouse signal?
cards.back: A lit green arrow on a doghouse signal gives a protected turn with conflicting traffic stopped, while the green light lets you turn only after oncoming traffic clears.

cards.front: What does a yellow light or yellow arrow mean on a doghouse signal?
cards.back: On a doghouse signal, a yellow light or yellow arrow means red is coming, so stop unless you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely; if already in, finish the turn with care once traffic is clear.

cards.front: What does a steady green arrow mean?
cards.back: A steady green arrow means oncoming traffic is stopped and you may go the arrow's way with caution, still yielding to pedestrians in the intersection.

cards.front: How is the flashing yellow arrow signal built, and why?
cards.back: The flashing yellow arrow left-turn signal uses four separate lenses, a design federal highway research found moves traffic more efficiently and cuts crash chances.

cards.front: What does a solid red arrow mean?
cards.back: A solid red arrow means stop and do not turn until the signal changes.

cards.front: What does a solid yellow arrow warn?
cards.back: A solid yellow arrow warns the left-turn signal is about to turn red; stop if approaching, but if already in the intersection with no conflicting traffic you may finish the turn.

cards.front: When may you turn on a flashing yellow arrow?
cards.back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic, which has a green light, and after checking for a safe gap and for crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.

cards.front: What does a solid green arrow mean on the flashing yellow arrow signal?
cards.back: A solid green arrow means oncoming traffic is stopped and you may turn left, still yielding to people in the crosswalk; with detection cameras or sensors this phase may be skipped when no one is waiting to turn.

decks.domain: Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals

cards.front: What do pedestrian signals do, and what do some show?
cards.back: Pedestrian signals control crossing points, and some show audible or visual countdowns of the time left.

cards.front: What does WALK mean, and what about when it flashes?
cards.back: A walking person symbol or WALK means traffic must yield and pedestrians may cross; when it starts flashing, those already crossing should finish.

cards.front: What does DONT WALK or a raised hand mean?
cards.back: DONT WALK or a red raised hand means do not cross, and drivers must always yield to pedestrians.

cards.front: What is a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon?
cards.back: A Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon is a crossing device that warns drivers of pedestrians, and its signal sequence has six steps.

recap_hooks.text: Fog lines and solid white lines are not for crossing; double solid white is prohibited.
Stop behind the stop line or crosswalk, or before the intersection if neither exists.
Lane arrows show the moves allowed from each lane.
Bike lanes are for bikes only; green paint flags conflict points.
Broken yellow allows passing when safe; solid on your side or double solid forbids it.
The center turn lane serves lefts both ways, never passing or merging.
A Michigan Left means go straight or right, then U-turn at the crossover.
Stop behind yield lines; triangles mean yield to pedestrians.
Never cut through a lot to get around a signal.
Red stops, yellow means stop if you safely can, green goes with caution.
Flashing red is a stop, flashing yellow is go carefully, and a dark signal is an all-way stop.
A green arrow protects your turn; a green light means yield first.
A flashing yellow arrow means yield to oncoming traffic before turning.
WALK means cross, the raised hand means do not, and drivers always yield to pedestrians.
